$comment: PRE-REGISTERED adoption gate for is_circumstantial v2. Committed BEFORE any blind label exists and before the classifier's author has seen a single rating. Same rule as pass_bars.json and v3_expected_shape.json: a criterion written after seeing the agreement figure is not a criterion. Changing anything here is its own explicit commit that says why.
what_is_being_decided: whether the state_coverage denominator moves from is_circumstantial v1 (first person + factual marker) to v2 (first person + a term the persona's P/B/J facts carry that no offered graph fact does).

adoption_criterion.rule: v2 is adopted IFF it agrees with the blind labels BETTER than v1 does, over the same 53 segments.
adoption_criterion.why_comparative: an absolute figure is uninterpretable. 'v2 agrees 85%' means nothing without knowing whether v1 agrees 70% or 90%, and the question on the table is not whether v2 is good but whether it is better than what ships today.
report: simple agreement for v1 and for v2
Cohen's kappa for v1 and for v2, because the classes are unbalanced and raw agreement flatters a classifier that mostly says the majority class
every disagreement, BOTH directions, enumerated with its segment text
adoption_criterion.read_the_disagreements: a v2 miss that is a principled edge case is a different object from one that is a hole in the definition. The enumeration is not decoration; it is how that distinction gets made.
adoption_criterion.clustering_clause: if v2 beats v1 but its misses CLUSTER in one identifiable class, that class is recorded as a NAMED LIMITATION of instrument v2 — never as a silent tolerance, and never fixed by editing the classifier until it stops missing them, which would be fitting to the labels.
adoption_criterion.canary_compatibility: AN ADOPTION CRITERION, NOT A COURTESY. An instrument must leave test_the_state_lever_collapses_state_coverage able to fire on the EXISTING fixture. If it zeroes the fixture's circumstantial count it FAILS adoption regardless of sheet performance. v2.1 failed exactly here and was reverted. v2.2 catching 'I cannot always get myself to the clinic' follows from the ability frame in the inventory, so this should be free — and free-and-asserted is the difference between a rule and a hope.

metric_split.rule: instrument v2 reports TWO numbers, never one.
metric_split.state_coverage: over circumstantial segments that a P/B/J id COULD cover.
metric_split.schema_gap_rate: share of circumstantial segments that no id in the declared surface can cover.
metric_split.derivation: from principle, not from the eight segments that raised it: a coverage metric computed over segments nothing in the schema can express measures the SCHEMA, not the model. Blending the two produces a number that falls when the model gets worse and also when the surface gets narrower, and cannot say which happened.
metric_split.known_uncoverable_class: symptoms. PROFILE_FIELDS does not carry them and biomarkers are deliberately outside it, so 'I feel breathless most days' asserts a circumstance with no available id. That is a coverage finding to log, exactly as the module docstring already says for an unsimulated persona's missing event log.
metric_split.who_adjudicates: the labels. The rater labels the CONCEPT — does this segment assert a fact about the speaker's own circumstances, and could the declared surface support it — and the classifier's job is to approximate that, never to define it.

floors_are_instrument_relative.rule: a coverage floor is stamped with the instrument version it was registered against, and does not transfer across an instrument change.

v3_floor.status: unchanged, and v0.4 remains adjudicated under it

floors_are_instrument_relative.consequence: v2 reading 0.6000 on the v3 cassette is NOT a pass against the v3 floor. It is a number from a different denominator that happens to land on the old bar, which is the most suspicious shape a rewritten metric can take and is reported as a coincidence rather than a result.
floors_are_instrument_relative.before_v4: adopting v2 re-registers the floor against the label-validated denominator, in its own commit, BEFORE any v4 run exists. A bar that silently survives an instrument change is a bar that means nothing.

conflicts_of_interest.consequence: the author cannot rate. Labels come from an independent rater working from segment text alone — no personas, no citations, no kinds, no classifier verdicts — so the validation cannot inherit the classifier's token-match logic.
conflicts_of_interest.sheet: 53 segments, hash-shuffled so the classes are not grouped.

amendments.what: v2 adopted on the comparative criterion, then immediately superseded as a CANDIDATE by v2.1; adoption of v2.1 requires HELD-OUT labels, and no floor is set under any biased instrument.
amendments.why_v2_is_not_shipped_into_v4: v2's two validated miss classes are own-regimen segments and shared-circumstance-term compounds. The compound class is exactly the population v4's schema lever is designed to act on: if finer segmentation splits 'I work shifts, so evening slots would help' into two segments, the circumstance half is the kind v2 drops. Running v4 under v2 would measure the treatment with an instrument blind in the treated region, so the correction is the experiment's precondition rather than optional pre-work.
amendments.v21_definition: the subtraction applies only OUTSIDE a possession/experience frame. A term inside such a frame is asserted about the speaker, so graph overlap does not disqualify it — 'metformin' in 'I take metformin' is circumstance, the same token in 'metformin can cause nausea' is not. Operationalises the rater's committed R1; derived from the rules, not from the fifteen misses.
amendments.in_sample_is_reported_not_relied_on: scoring v2.1 against the 53 labels that motivated it is in-sample by construction. It reads agreement 0.8462, kappa 0.4639 against v2's 0.6923 / 0.3113. Reported, labelled in-sample, and NOT the adoption evidence.

held_out_design.source: tests/cassettes/archive/narration_battery.20260823T170152Z — the prompt-v2 cassette, 30 takes, 63 unique segments. Different text, same model.
held_out_design.protocol: the rater labels the sheet blind by the same five decision rules before seeing any classifier verdict; v2.1 is adopted on those numbers under the same comparative criterion and the same clustering clause.
held_out_design.mapping: each archived take maps to a battery case by question text (30/30 verified), so per-persona state terms and per-case graph terms are recoverable for scoring.

amendments.rater_blinding_disclosure: NEAR-TOTAL, NOT TOTAL. The rater has previously seen a handful of prompt-v2 cassette excerpts quoted in reports (a bus segment, a medication list). Recorded here beside the classifier-author conflict rather than left implicit, because a disclosed partial blind is evidence and an undisclosed one is not. ADDITIONALLY: the held-out sheet carries prompt-v2 inline-marker debris (trailing 'Fact 190' / 'Fact_ids: [...]' on three segments). The rater is instructed to rate the sentence and ignore it, and discloses that the debris itself un-blinds slightly — it marks those segments as v2-era takes and hints they were factual-kind.

rater_pre_commitments.no_new_rules_mid_sheet: the rater labels by R1-R5 verbatim. A segment forcing a distinction the five rules do not cover gets '?' with its reason, never a rule minted on the spot — a rule invented on the validation set contaminates it exactly as a definition tuned on it would. If the '?' pile CLUSTERS, that cluster becomes the next rule, adopted before whatever sheet comes after.
rater_pre_commitments.consistency_probe: near-duplicate pairs are labelled independently as encountered and their agreement reported. Unlike the first sheet the rater does not know which pairs exist, which makes it a better probe.

floor_decision.rule: NO floor is registered under an instrument with a known directional bias.
floor_decision.why: a floor under a biased instrument forces every future reader to carry a mental correction term, which is the blended-number failure in bar form.
floor_decision.floor: 0.6 is re-registered as a GOLD-SEMANTICS bar, attached to whichever instrument passes held-out validation, in its own commit before any v4 run.
floor_decision.anchor_sentence_for_the_v4_baseline_sect: v3 missed the floor under every defensible reading — shipped instrument, corrected instrument, and human labels — and the correction changed the size of the miss, not its existence.

bias_asymmetry.v2: denominator too SMALL (misses) -> inflates coverage. Observed 0.6000 against gold 0.5263.
bias_asymmetry.v21_in_sample: denominator too LARGE (false positives) -> deflates coverage. Observed 0.4762 against gold 0.5263.
bias_asymmetry.consequence: the two instruments are not symmetric risks. A floor registered against v2.1 is CONSERVATIVE: a pass under v2.1 implies a pass under gold, not the reverse. A floor under v2 would have been the opposite and would have passed runs gold fails.
bias_asymmetry.does_not_change_decision_1: the bar is still gold-semantics and the held-out gate still decides. Recorded here because the asymmetry belongs where the floor is.

superseded_by_unstable_bias.rule: the instrument's job is ESTIMATION with human-label audits at every version bump. It does not carry the floor.
superseded_by_unstable_bias.why: with the bias direction unstable across texts, no instrument-relative floor is conservative by construction, so an instrument-relative floor cannot be defended at all. The gold-semantics bar is the only defensible one.
superseded_by_unstable_bias.audit_obligation: each instrument version is scored against blind human labels on text it has not seen, and its deviation from the gold reading is reported as the estimate's error bar — not corrected for, reported.

schema_gap_rate_arm.why: the schema lever adds no symptom ids, so the uncoverable population should not move. A cheap no-effect arm that guards the one metric v4 must not touch.
schema_gap_rate_arm.if_it_moves: something other than the declared variable moved; investigate before reading state_coverage.

held_out_result.criterion: MET. v2.1 beats v1 on agreement and on kappa, held out.
held_out_result.in_sample_penalty: v2.1 kappa fell 0.4639 -> 0.3182 between in-sample and held-out, which is the gap the split was built to expose. v2's held-out kappa is EXACTLY 0.0 — chance.

named_limitations.BA1_locator_over_inclusion: 6 of 7 bare temporal-locator segments ('during my work hours') are called circumstantial. The rater's split between locator and asserted conflict is syntactic-pragmatic and a token matcher cannot see it. Single direction, as predicted before scoring. The asserted-conflict half is caught 6 of 6.
named_limitations.shared_term_under_inclusion: 8 coverable misses (03, 04, 12, 17, 19, 20, 25, 44) — cost, distance and transport circumstances whose terms the graph also carries and which sit outside a possession frame. Partly fixed by v2.1, not eliminated.
named_limitations.own_regimen: FIXED. 0 of 7 missed, against 8 of 8 missed under v2.

bias_direction_is_NOT_stable.finding: v2.1 over-counts the denominator on the v3 cassette (42 against gold 38) and UNDER-counts it here (38 counted against 42 labelled).
bias_direction_is_NOT_stable.consequence: the conservatism argument recorded under floor_decision.bias_asymmetry DOES NOT HOLD. A floor registered against v2.1 cannot be called conservative, because the sign of its bias changes with the text.
bias_direction_is_NOT_stable.status: supersedes the bias_asymmetry entry, which is kept as the record of what was believed when it was written.

adoption_blocked_by_the_canary.what_happened: v2.1 was wired into score() and the change was reverted. Under v2.1 the canary's baseline fixture contains ZERO circumstantial segments, so state_coverage reads 0.0 and test_the_state_lever_collapses_state_coverage cannot run.
adoption_blocked_by_the_canary.why_this_outranks_the_criterion: the canary is the mechanism that proves the metric can fail. An instrument whose denominator the canary cannot exercise is one the canary cannot validate. The pre-registration decided WHICH instrument, and never contemplated an adopted instrument that disables the failure test.
adoption_blocked_by_the_canary.note: the fixture text that v2.1 rejects ('I cannot always get myself to the clinic') is a plausible circumstance a human would label y — the same under-inclusion class as the 8 shared-term misses, surfacing in the canary rather than in the sheet.
adoption_blocked_by_the_canary.decision_required: rewrite the canary fixture so it asserts circumstance in a form v2.1 recognises and re-verify the lever collapses; or treat the canary failure as evidence v2.1's under-inclusion is too aggressive and iterate the definition. Rewriting a fixture so an adopted instrument passes its own failure test is not a decision to take quietly.

metric_restructure_question.asked: why is a CLASSIFIER recovering what the GENERATOR already knows? A segment citing B-transport is circumstantial by construction.
metric_restructure_question.answer: the restructure is NOT what the metric does. state_coverage is cited_circumstantial / total_circumstantial where BOTH come from the classifier's list, so a segment that cites a state id but is not flagged leaves the numerator AND the denominator.

measured_on_the_v3_cassette.finding: 3 to 5 genuinely grounded segments are invisible to the current metric under every instrument. That is a correctness defect, not a precision one: the metric can under-count grounding that the schema already proved.

metric_restructure_question.does_it_shrink_the_classifier_job: PARTLY, and less than hoped. The numerator becomes exact and classifier-free, which is the real win. But the residual — uncited circumstantial — is still 18 of 41 denominator entries at gold, so the classifier still determines about 44% of the denominator. Deviation from gold barely moves for v2.1 (-0.0501 current, -0.0499 restructured) and gets worse for v2.
metric_restructure_question.conclusion: do the restructure on correctness grounds. It does not remove the need for v2.2; it narrows what v2.2 must catch to uncited circumstance, which is exactly the three-sightings class.
metric_restructure_question.floor_note: gold reads 0.5610 restructured against 0.5263 current. BOTH miss 0.6. The anchor sentence holds under the restructure.

v22_protocol.the_sheets_are_spent: both existing sheets become IN-SAMPLE for v2.2 the moment its definition is written by anyone who has seen the 8 held-out misses. Scoring v2.2 on them and calling it a win would be in-sample dressed as held-out.
v22_protocol.definition_source: the expanded frame inventory is derived from R1-R5 and BA1-BA3, which already name the frames: possession, experience, ability, situation/distance, negated-resource. The misses told us the inventory was SHORT; they must not tell us what to put in it.
v22_protocol.scoring: both existing sheets scored and reported, labelled IN-SAMPLE.
v22_protocol.adoption_requires: a third sheet neither party has seen.
candidate_third_sheets: the v1-era cassette in the evidence bundle archive
v22_protocol.fallback_if_no_unseen_text_of_sufficient: pre-register v2.2's held-out sheet as the FIRST SLICE of v4's own output, scored before v4's headline numbers are computed, so the instrument is validated on the text it will actually measure.
v22_protocol.standing_rule: the switch stays unthrown until an instrument passes a sheet nobody has seen.

check_1_the_invisible_state_citing_segme.question: 23 segments cite a state id but gold's numerator is 20. Extraction gap, or decorative state citations?
check_1_the_invisible_state_citing_segme.answer: NEITHER, exactly. All three reached the rater. None was labelled n, so the predicted decorative class — a CLINICAL claim carrying a state id — does not exist in this cassette. What exists instead: two of the three are y? (circumstantial, nothing in the schema can cover it) AND THEY CITE A STATE ID ANYWAY.

the_three.18: abstention. 'I also keep a daily symptom diary...' cites P-medications.empagliflozin + four graph facts.
the_three.33: y? symptom claim ('I feel pretty breathless most days') citing P-condition and P-stage.
the_three.40: y? symptom claim ('hot flushes... joints ache') citing P-medications.anastrozole and P-medications.tamoxifen.

check_1_the_invisible_state_citing_segme.what_it_means: GAP-CITING. The model reaches for the nearest available id when none fits: there is no symptom id, so a symptom claim gets P-condition or the drug that causes it. That is the schema gap manifesting as citation displacement — the same mechanism as the f_recall displacement finding, one level down.
check_1_the_invisible_state_citing_segme.consequence_for_the_restructure: a numerator of 'all state-citing segments' would count 33 and 40 as GROUNDED while the labels place them in the schema gap. The inflation path arrives through y?, not through n.
check_1_the_invisible_state_citing_segme.decision: the restructured numerator is adopted WITH state_citation_aptness as a named diagnostic: of the segments citing a state id, the share a rater judges the citation actually grounds. Audited against labels at every version bump, reported beside the coverage figure and never folded into it. Label-adjudicated gap-citing segments are excluded from the numerator and counted in schema_gap_rate, which is where the labels already put them.

check_2_extraction_audit.question: were the sheets filtered by anything classifier-derived?
check_2_extraction_audit.answer: NO. Both were exhaustive. Sheet 1: 53 segments from every case, no filter, sheet size identical to the extraction. Sheet 2: 63 parsed segments, 63 unique, no dedup loss.
check_2_extraction_audit.consequence: gold is gold over the cassette, not over a filtered sheet, and the 23-vs-20 gap is NOT an extraction gap. The in-sample deviations from gold stand as stated.
check_2_extraction_audit.standing_rule: exhaustive extraction — every segment of every take, hash-shuffled, no filter — for every future sheet.

check_3_third_sheet.source: the v1-era cassette at git 1c07e78 (prompt v1, 25 takes, qwen2.5:7b-instruct). 57 unique segments, all takes parsed.
check_3_third_sheet.exposure_handling: the five v0.1 bundle-sampled takes were read in full during the v1 session. Their archived form carries NO segment text — the v0.1 CaseResult schema did not store it — so exposed segments cannot be identified individually. Excluded by CASE instead, which is the conservative move: all 7 segments belonging to the five exposed case_ids are removed.
check_3_third_sheet.distribution_shift: v1-era text carries the double-contract era's tics. Accepted for ADOPTION because the estimation-with-audits rule dissolves the dilemma: this sheet is the adoption gate on unseen text available now, and the v4 run carries its own fresh audit slice, labelled before the headline is computed, validating the instrument on the distribution it actually measures.
check_3_third_sheet.the_fallback_is_now_standing: v4's first slice stops being a fallback and becomes the per-run audit.

gap_citing_prediction.registered_before: v2.2 exists and before any v4 run
gap_citing_prediction.mechanism: v4's segmentation lever forces MORE segments to carry citations. Symptom and experience segments still have no apt id. A model obligated to cite with nothing apt to cite reaches for the nearest state id — which is what segments 33 and 40 already do voluntarily under v3.
gap_citing_prediction.prediction: state_citation_aptness FALLS at v4, and/or the gap-citing count RISES. Direction registered now so the number cannot be read backwards later.
gap_citing_prediction.why_this_registration_matters: without it, a falling aptness figure at v4 reads as the model getting worse. It is the metric finally seeing a gap the schema always had.

schema_gap_rate_arm_amended.was: expected roughly flat, because the schema lever adds no symptom ids
schema_gap_rate_arm_amended.still_true_at: the POPULATION level — the set of segments nothing can cover does not change size because of a segmentation change
schema_gap_rate_arm_amended.but: gap members can MOVE BETWEEN BUCKETS under citation pressure: uncited-circumstantial becomes gap-citing. Measured only as the uncited bucket, the flat prediction can fail for a bookkeeping reason.
schema_gap_rate_arm_amended.amendment: the schema gap is measured as the UNION of both manifestations — uncited circumstantial with no apt id, plus gap-citing segments. That union is what is expected flat.

aptness_blinding_protocol.problem: aptness — does this id's referent make this claim true of the speaker — REQUIRES seeing the citation, so it cannot ride along on the circumstantiality pass, which must not see it.
aptness_blinding_protocol.protocol: TWO PASSES, ONE SHEET, ORDER FIXED. Pass 1: circumstantiality, text only, blind, by R1-R5 and BA1-BA3. Pass 2: over the state-citing subset ONLY, citations revealed, aptness judged against namespace semantics. Pass 1 labels are submitted before pass 2 begins.
aptness_blinding_protocol.why_the_order_is_load_bearing: reversed or merged, the citation leaks into the circumstantial call. Three instruments have now been spent learning what leakage costs.

v22_construction_constraint.rule: each of the five frames gets its own unit fixture sentence, AUTHORED FROM THE RULE, asserted before the classifier is run on any sheet.

fixtures.ability: I cannot get myself to Z
fixtures.situation: the site is far from me

v22_construction_constraint.why: the canary principle at unit level — every frame watched to fire before any aggregate is computed. It makes the ability-frame-passes-the-canary claim free-and-asserted from birth rather than discovered at the gate.

v22_in_sample.status: IN-SAMPLE ON BOTH SHEETS. Not adoption evidence. The v1-era sheet decides.
v22_in_sample.reading: v2.2 is slightly WORSE than v2.1 on sheet 1 and much better on sheet 2. That is the expected shape: sheet 1 is where v2.1's definition was written, so v2.1's sheet-1 figures were inflated by the same in-sample effect this row is labelled for. v2.2 trades a little sheet-1 performance for consistency — 0.83/0.83 against 0.85/0.68.
v22_in_sample.BA1_locator_false_positives: down from 6 of 7 under v2.1 to 2 of 7 under v2.2, with 5 of 6 asserted conflicts still caught.
v22_in_sample.canary: PASSES by construction — the ability frame fires on the fixture sentence, asserted in tests/test_frames.py rather than discovered at the gate.

restructured_with_aptness_exclusion_on_t.note: both miss the 0.6 floor. The anchor sentence survives the restructure AND the aptness exclusion.

ADOPTION.sheet: 50 segments from the v1-era cassette (git 1c07e78), exhaustive extraction minus 5 exposed cases, 49 scored — segment 48 excluded as a documented rule collision. Held out from EVERY instrument, so this is the one comparison on genuinely equal footing.
ADOPTION.criterion: MET on both metrics, and canary compatibility was asserted from birth by the ability fixture rather than discovered here.

predicted_zones.modal_wall: 1 of 8 flagged. The experience frame implements BA2 rather than approximating it.
predicted_zones.possession_embedded_in_clinical: 1 of 3 missed (33). The frame is not anchored to sentence-initial position.

named_limitation_the_minimal_pair_found.test: segment 37 here (modal bisoprolol, labelled n) against held-out 00 (indicative bisoprolol, labelled y?) — same drug, same effects, different mood.
named_limitation_the_minimal_pair_found.result: v2.2 does NOT split the pair. It calls both circumstantial, so it is correct on 00 and wrong on 37.
named_limitation_the_minimal_pair_found.diagnosis: the modal suppression guards the EXPERIENCE frame only. Modal clinical text carrying a possessive ('my hands', 'my heartbeat') still fires the POSSESSION frame, so BA2 is enforced on one frame and bypassed through another.
named_limitation_the_minimal_pair_found.direction: one-way over-inclusion on modal text containing possessives.
named_limitation_the_minimal_pair_found.status: NAMED LIMITATION, not patched. Extending the modal suppression across frames after seeing which item it fails is fitting to the adoption sheet, and the adoption sheet is now spent for that purpose. It becomes v2.3's registered target, validated on a sheet nobody has seen.

v3_final_rescoring.reading: v3 misses the 0.6 floor under the adopted instrument as it did under every other. Instrument history: v1 0.5135, v2 0.6000, v2.1 0.4762, v2.2 0.4419, human labels 0.5263.

ADOPTION.anchor_sentence: v3 missed the floor under every defensible reading — shipped instrument, corrected instrument, adopted instrument, and human labels — and the correction changed the size of the miss, not its existence.

GOLD_FLOOR.registered_before: the v4 pre-registration and any v4 run
GOLD_FLOOR.semantics: GOLD. The bar is answered against blind human labels on an audited slice, never against an instrument's full-run estimate.
GOLD_FLOOR.why_not_instrument_relative: the bias sign of an instrument has already flipped once across texts — v2 over-reported, v2.1 under-reported, v2.2 under-reports on this cassette by 0.084. A floor attached to an estimator whose error changes direction with the text is a bar that means something different each time it is read.

the_instrument_estimates_and_is_audited.deviation_direction: under-inclusion, via the modal-plus-possessive door the minimal pair found
the_instrument_estimates_and_is_audited.obligation: every run carries an audit slice, labelled blind BEFORE any aggregate is read. The audit measures the estimator's error on that run's own text; it is reported, not corrected for.

v3_baseline_registered_for_v4.anchor: v3 missed the floor under every defensible reading — shipped instrument, corrected instrument, adopted instrument, and human labels — and the correction changed the size of the miss, not its existence.

LAW_estimator_validity_is_distribution_r.statement: Estimator validity is DISTRIBUTION-RELATIVE. Any lever that changes the output distribution silently re-opens every instrument validated on the old one.

the_measurement.adopted: is_circumstantial_v22, adopted on a held-out sheet at agreement 0.6939 / kappa 0.3336
the_measurement.finding: THE ADOPTED INSTRUMENT WAS BEATEN BY THE ONE IT REPLACED, on the run's own text. Denominator error -12: v2.2 counted 17 circumstantial where blind labels say 29.
the_measurement.mechanism: v2.2's frames were validated on multi-clause text. The SPLIT lever changed the distribution to short single-claim segments, and the estimator's error moved with it. This is not a v2.2 defect; it is a property of validating an instrument on one distribution and running it on another.

structural_consequences.adoption_is_per_distribution_not_permane: an instrument's validation carries a DISTRIBUTION STAMP — prompt version and grain statistics (mean_segments_per_take, single_segment_rate) — and EXPIRES when a lever moves them. An adoption record without a distribution stamp is a claim about text nobody named.
structural_consequences.per_run_audit_is_promoted: from 'a check on the estimate' to 'the mechanism that detects instrument expiry'. It did exactly that on its first exercise: without it, state_coverage 0.5 would have shipped as the v4 figure with no sign the instrument had degraded on the text it was measuring.

the_three_failure_modes_now_all_demonstr: pre-registration catches MOTIVATED READING — a prediction written after the numbers
canaries catch DEAD INSTRUMENTS — a metric that cannot fail
per-run audits catch TRUE INSTRUMENTS DYING QUIETLY OF DISTRIBUTION SHIFT — an instrument that was valid, still looks valid, and is no longer measuring what it measured

v23_brief.inverted: v2.3 was queued to fix the modal-plus-possessive door, a MULTI-CLAUSE pathology. The audit says the live problem is the opposite end: under-counting on SHORT SINGLE-CLAIM segments, -12 on the denominator.
v23_brief.registered_target: BOTH doors, with the distribution stamp deciding which dominates for a given run.

held_out_sheet.source: the 15 UNAUDITED takes of the v4 run — 33 unique segments
held_out_sheet.why_it_is_the_natural_sheet: unseen by the rater and by every instrument, and it is the same distribution the instrument will measure. Distribution-matched held-out text is now a requirement rather than a convenience, per the law above.

v23_brief.open_design_question: whether v2.3 stays a five-frame classifier grown two doors, or restructures the residual detector around SEGMENT LENGTH as a first-class feature. HELD until the failure table on the audit sheet localises which door cost the 12 — the count alone does not.

the_three_faces_of_one_question: F3: identical claim shapes intermittently grounded — 'I take metformin, empagliflozin and semaglutide' cites nothing while the four-drug segment cites all four
the instrument under-counting on those same short segments
gap-citing as causal-neighbour fallback, now at a measured 4 of 14
v5_direction.the_question: when the model CAN cite correctly, what makes it actually do so every time?
v5_direction.lever_class: decoding / prompt consistency — NOT a schema lever, so v5 like v4 risks no structural guarantee
v5_direction.parked_but_real: the gap story — symptoms, negatives, B-silence. F5's zero-barrier-citations question unseals with the full run; if barriers truly never speak, that is the expressiveness thread's next pull, AFTER reliability, because F3 says reliability is where the coverage points are.
